clue.text: Card game — George's victim makes a bloomer

parts.note: snap is the children's card game of calling out matching cards
Saint George is the legendary slayer of a dragon

explanation.surface: A card game ends with somebody named George committing a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' reads as a blunder; here it is a plant that blooms, the garden flower also called antirrhinum.
explanation.definitionFit: The antirrhinum is a common garden flower, and anything that flowers is a bloomer.

clue.text: Announce no forthcoming changes in shade

indicators.note: letters that change go into a different order
the word no comes forth, out of Announce, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Someone declares that no changes are coming in a colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forthcoming' takes NO out of ANNOUNCE, leaving ANUNCE; 'changes' shuffles that.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle gradation of meaning or colour, a fine shade.

clue.text: G & S game

definitions.meaning: an operetta by Gilbert and Sullivan, the one about aesthetic poets
the solitaire card game played alone

explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote an operetta of this title, and it is also the British name for solitaire, a one-player card game.

clue.text: Restraint for sheep that's falling down

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a shackle is a fetter or restraint

explanation.surface: A farmer needs a tether for a sheep that keeps collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling down' is the definition, of a building, not a sheep falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramshackle building is dilapidated, in a state of disrepair.

clue.text: Light source — big bang in space

indicators.note: the bang goes inside the space

parts.note: a gap is a space
a slam is a loud bang, as of a door

explanation.surface: A lamp's origin is the cosmic Big Bang in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big bang in space' suggests cosmology, but it is SLAM inside GAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A street lamp burning coal gas was a Victorian source of light.

clue.text: First of all, not everyone wants such information

indicators.note: the first letter of each of all the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Not every reader wants this sort of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of recent events are information.

clue.text: But no saints in that of Newgate

definitions.text: But no saints in that of Newgate

parts.words: But no saints in that of Newgate
parts.note: a church listing of saints' days contrasts with the famous Newgate record of notorious criminals, which held no saints

explanation.surface: London's old Newgate prison register held sinners, not saints.
explanation.walkthrough: The Newgate Calendar was an 18th-19th century chronicle of crimes from Newgate, London's main prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A church year lists saints' days; the Newgate one, of the same name, listed felons.

clue.text: Not dated Dec 25th

definitions.meaning: modern, current, not out of date
Christmas Day, when gifts are given

explanation.definitionFit: Something contemporary belongs to our own time; Christmas is a day for gifts.

clue.text: Rice sent back when the French introduced cake

indicators.note: the French article is brought into the middle of the turned-round word
something sent back goes the other way, so the word Rice is read from its end

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: Rice pudding is returned to the kitchen and the French serve pastry instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns RICE into ECIR, and 'introduced' puts LA inside it: EC-LA-IR.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger filled with cream and topped with chocolate is a kind of small cake.

clue.text: They recreate dad's paper

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, with the possessive s kept
The Times is the newspaper in which this very puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: Somebody's father reads his daily newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They recreate' is a verb phrase: hobbies are things that provide recreation, so they 're-create' a tired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbies and amusements give relaxation, the literal sense of recreation.

clue.text: Languid, unlike Koko

definitions.meaning: Ko-Ko, the Lord High Executioner in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, sings 'I've got a little list', so someone unlike him has no list

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking energy fits languid; and Ko-Ko keeps a famous little list, so one without a list is his opposite.

clue.text: He has chapter and verse ending in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are jumbled together into a new order
the ending of the word verse is its final letter

explanation.surface: A scholar knows his Bible chapter and verse, but finishes muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes E from 'verse'; 'in confusion' shuffles AND with it. 'Chapter' is not a Bible division but a cathedral's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a cathedral presides over its chapter of canons.

clue.text: Get facts about East Side ' right — they're needed

indicators.note: the facts go around the other pieces

parts.note: data are facts
E is the compass abbreviation for east
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reporter gathers facts about New York's East Side.
explanation.walkthrough: DATA splits D...ATA around ESIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata is Latin for things desired, wanted or required.

clue.text: Temper made victim in 1 ac fight at last

indicators.note: to temper something is to mix or blend it, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the victim in the clue at 1 across is Saint George's dragon

explanation.surface: A rage turned somebody into a victim, and the fight came at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like anger but signals mixing: MADE and DRAGON are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation it names the site of the final battle at the end of the world, the fight to end all.

clue.text: A kind of break getting vegetables on credit

parts.note: greens are leafy green vegetables
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A shopper gets vegetables on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the link: GREENS on (placed before) TICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenstick fracture is a partial bone fracture, common in children.

clue.text: Tear mended in blue, with stripes

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for blue

parts.note: the sky is blue, a common crossword equivalence

indicators.note: something mended is put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rip in a blue garment is repaired, leaving it striped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mended' turns TEAR into TREA, and 'in' puts that inside SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky describes something marked with lines or bands, like streaky bacon.

clue.text: Name that's for remembrance

definitions.meaning: Ophelia in Hamlet: 'There's ..., that's for remembrance'

explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's given name and the herb Ophelia associates with memory.

clue.text: Did up engine from York in Lancaster's colour

indicators.note: the York word sits inside the Lancastrian colour

parts.note: the House of Lancaster's emblem was the red rose
Ebor, from the Latin Eboracum, is the short name for York, used in the Archbishop's signature

explanation.surface: A mechanic from York rebuilds an engine in the red of rival Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses set Lancaster (red rose) against York (white rose), so a Yorkshireman in red is the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebore an engine is to enlarge and smooth its worn cylinders during an overhaul.

clue.text: Turn the scale, not in vocal manner

parts.note: someone not in is out

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a way is a manner, a method

explanation.surface: Someone tips the balance by quiet means rather than speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocal' makes WAY sound like WEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in weight is to tip a balance, turning the scale.

clue.text: Get rid of those old investments

definitions.text: Get rid of those old investments

parts.words: Get rid of those old investments
parts.note: investments is read as vestments, clothes one is invested with, so the act is shedding garments, not selling shares

explanation.surface: A shareholder sells off outdated holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: Financial investments mislead; 'invest' also means to clothe in robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off one's robes or clothes is to strip.

clue.text: No credit is given, unfortunately, for caution

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately are wrong, so the letters fall into another order

explanation.surface: A lender refuses credit, sadly, as a precaution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' belongs to the fodder: NOCREDITIS has the ten letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence and wariness in action or speech is a synonym of caution.

clue.text: With eyes you see other people

indicators.note: what you can see is in plain view inside the words With eyes

explanation.surface: Someone observes that eyes are how we see.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'wiTH EYes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for unnamed others, as in 'they say', means other people in general.

clue.text: Flight of French Art head

parts.note: es is French for 'art' as in 'thou art' (tu es)
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone leads a flight of French art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb form of 'are', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away from danger or confinement is a flight.

clue.text: Mind sapper

definitions.meaning: to mind is to bear in mind, keep in memory
a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers (RE)

explanation.definitionFit: Bearing something in mind is recalling it; and a sapper is an RE soldier, read as RE plus member.

clue.text: Orders dentist to take one in

indicators.note: the dentist's letters take in the numeral, holding it

parts.note: BDS, Bachelor of Dental Surgery, is a dentist's qualification
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone instructs a dentist to see one more patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid someone do a thing is to command it, so bids are orders.

clue.text: Starting with one drink taken in by mouth

indicators.note: the pieces are taken into the word for mouth, which encloses them

parts.note: oral means of the mouth
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone begins by sipping a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ORAL is an adjective for the mouth; I and GIN go inside it. 'Starting' is the adjective, as in a starting position.
explanation.definitionFit: Original can mean initial or first in order, as an original plan is the starting one.

clue.text: Yarn half of them studied

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: Half of the group studied a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes TH from 'them'. 'Yarn' is the spun fibre here, not a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun fibre for sewing or knitting is yarn, also called thread.

clue.text: If he's taken something corruptly, he's a crook

indicators.note: corrupted text is garbled, so the letters are jumbled into new order

explanation.surface: Anyone who takes something dishonestly is a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: IFHESTAKEN gives the ten letters; the apostrophe in 'he's' adds none.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty robber who steals stealthily without violence is one kind of criminal.
